summary: SSE segment gaps and partial outputs after client reconnect behind proxy backoff
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports truncated SSE streams with missing middle segments after a short client disconnect. Problem appears only when their requests flow through a partner edge proxy that performs exponential backoff/retries.

Impact:
- Multiple customers inside LexiDocs observed partial documents (gaps in the middle of generated text) on ~15% of streaming responses for chat use-case.
- User-visible corruption in the middle of outputs causes product UX regression and manual customer workarounds.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod) -> requests routed via partner edge-proxy (regional PoP) -> us-east inference cluster.
- Models: redwood-open-7b-v2 primary, redwood-compat-3b fallback.
- Customer uses reserved dedicated capacity.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Client opens SSE stream to /v1/generate with keepalive toggles enabled and limited window for reconnects.
2) Introduce a short connection interruption at the edge (2-6s) while the model is mid-generation.
3) Partner proxy retries the connection using exponential backoff and reattaches to Redwood endpoint.
4) Client resumes stream using the resume token; server delivers continuation but a sequence of tokens in the middle are missing or replaced by an empty final chunk.

Observed behavior:
- The resumed stream sometimes contains a contiguous gap in the middle of the choice where tokens between offsets N and M are absent.
- Resume metadata shows ctx_offset advanced past the missing range (resume offset mismatch).
- No 5xx errors recorded on the Redwood side; edge-proxy logs show a retry that truncated the original TCP flow and reconnected without preserving the full streaming window.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should replay or continue from the last acknowledged token index; no tokens should be silently dropped.

Logs / Attachments:
- Edge proxy trace (attachment from customer): edge-trace-lexidocs-2026-03-09.log
- Sample SSE transcripts (customer-provided) showing gap markers.
- Instrumentation traces from api-gateway (request IDs included in comments).

Customer notes:
- This behavior started after partner updated their proxy to change idle read timeouts + aggressive backoff.
- LexiDocs cannot bypass partner PoP without significant network changes; they requested a fix or mitigation on Redwood side.
comments: Support - Sofia Alvarez (2026-03-10): Acknowledged customer report and opened this ticket. Collected sample transcripts and asked for edge proxy logs and request IDs. Provided initial workaround suggestion to increase client reconnect window.

Customer - LexiDocs SRE (2026-03-10): Provided edge-proxy trace and three sample SSE transcripts with request IDs: rwd-req-3345, rwd-req-3372, rwd-req-3410. Noted partner changed proxy behavior on 2026-03-08.

Eng (Maya Chen) (2026-03-11): Started triage. Reproduced internally by simulating a proxy reconnect that performs TCP close+reopen and observed resume offset advancing without replay. Hypothesis: proxy retry causes server-side prefix cache to be bypassed and session resume logic treats new socket as separate stream, advancing offsets when client resumes. Added logging around resume token validation.

SRE (Hussein Patel) (2026-03-11): Confirmed no 5xx from inference nodes; api-gateway logs show two different connection IDs for same logical request when proxy retries. Captured gateway traces: trace-us-3345 and trace-us-3410.

Support - Sofia Alvarez (2026-03-12): Shared temporary mitigation with customer: disable partner proxy retries for streaming endpoints or configure proxy to preserve long-lived TCP streams (recommended). Customer requested Redwood-side mitigations because partner change is not possible short-term.

Eng (Maya Chen) (2026-03-12): Implemented additional resume verification header parsing in a dev branch. Created PR for more robust resume token mapping to persistent session IDs (see related_github_prs). Will test in staging with simulated proxy behavior.
investigation_notes: Repro: Simulating TCP close+reopen at edge causes gateway to assign a new connection id; resume flow uses client-supplied resume token but server-side cache lookup checks for persistent session id, mismatch leads to continuation from a later offset.
Hypothesis: partner backoff that tears down TCP connections prevents the gateway from retaining incremental streaming state tied to connection lifecycle.

Evidence: gateway logs show ctx_offset advanced by the size of last-inflight buffer and resume tokens match client, but internal session mapping resolves to a newer ephemeral session. No model-side token loss detected; server produced full sequence but parts not forwarded back to original client stream.
Risk: Changes to resume behavior must not allow duplicate token emission or double-replay; need end-to-end tests across SSE and WS with proxy tear scenarios.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: Customer can disable proxy retries for streaming route or extend idle timeouts to avoid mid-generation TCP tear-downs. Documented recommended proxy settings and a draft support KB.
Short-term engineering fix: Added extra mapping to persist session ids across reconnections when a valid resume token is presented. Deployed to staging for validation (branch: session-resume-fix).

Planned follow-ups: Roll out change to a subset of serving nodes behind feature-flag; run roster test with partner proxy simulation. Track metrics for resumed-stream success rate and partial-drop rate. Create post-deploy verification playbook and update Streaming Resume Runbook.
